project.title: Three Scoped Contraction Results: Quadratic, Convex, and Affine Scalar Regimes
project.venue_rubric_source: Official ICLR 2027 AuthorGuidelines and ReviewerGuidelines (manager-verified); local ICLR 2026 discrete review rubric remains an internal scoring schema only
project.paper_identity: A theory-only scoped exposition of three separate results: fixed-quadratic exposure products, ambient-Hessian gradient-descent contraction, and an affine conditional-mean recursion. It makes no comparator-path, intervention, unlearning, empirical, deployment, or novelty claim.

blockers: The original baseline remains frozen and non-self-contained; revision_01 packages identified TeX dependencies only under manuscript/.
Historical public-baseline numerical and method claims lack co-located scripts, outputs, configurations, and preregistration records; they are not asserted in revision_01.
The remote snapshot is a different paper.tex SHA-256 and cannot silently supply evidence or text to the public baseline.
No deployment-visible enable signal has been validated to distinguish natural harmful/noisy data from benign-hard/valueful data across two real scenarios.

The Round-2 meta-review sets the current-evidence ceiling at 2: T1--T3 remain only a scoped exposition of separate elementary results, with no demonstrated theorem-level distinction from direct optimization/stochastic-recursion antecedents, nontrivial unification, or empirical capability.

Further manuscript-only iteration is stopped. Resumption requires either the U3 matched two-trajectory, time-ordered data-block perturbation theorem with a material antecedent distinction and falsifier, or a new claim-linked reproducible experiment; the existing historical and remote material cannot supply that evidence.
